statement: You are given an integer array values. Replace every element with its rank and return the resulting array.
Ranks start at 1 for the smallest value and grow by 1 for each next larger distinct value. Equal elements get the same rank, so the ranks have no gaps.
One approach: pop the values from a min-heap (or sort them), give each new distinct value the next rank in a map, then look up every original element in that map.

examples.explanation: The distinct values in order are 2, 6, 15, 20, 26 and 98, which get ranks 1 to 6. Both 2s get rank 1.
There are five distinct values, 10 to 50 in steps of 10, so they get ranks 1 to 5. Each repeated value keeps its rank, so the largest rank is 5, not 8.
All elements are equal, so they all share rank 1.
